prompt: A shell runs this command line, where `/nope` does not exist. Where does the error message from `ls` go?
choices: On the terminal; out.txt is empty
The shell reports a syntax error
explain: `>` redirects only file descriptor 1 (standard output). `ls` writes its error to descriptor 2 (standard error), which was not redirected, so the message still appears on the terminal and `out.txt` ends up empty. To capture it you would add `2>`.
